post_text:
Scaling felt safe. Then the metrics lied.
I was certain we had the scaling model locked down for the Auth service. We optimized heavily and the P95 latency looked beautiful: flat, fast.
I assumed that P95 latency was the ultimate indicator of user experience.
The Black Friday wave hit. Traffic spiked 300%. 🚀
Our main alerts screamed, but not for latency. Upstream services started issuing massive 504 timeouts.
I stared at the dashboard. P95 was holding steady at 45ms. How was the system crumbling with perfect observed performance? 💀
The contradiction was jarring. Production was actively failing, yet the primary metric we used to define success looked green.
We dove deep. Hours later, we found the killer: massive, full-stop Garbage Collection pauses. The service was spending 80% of its time cleaning heap, not serving requests.
The request timer only measured the time inside the processing thread, ignoring the CPU stall caused by GC. 🧠
We had been horizontally scaling replicas based on a metric that masked critical resource exhaustion.
That required an emergency on-call rotation and a complex rollback plan involving the load balancer configuration.
The Moral 👇
The quality of a system metric is defined by what it explicitly excludes.
